scenarios.label: Production app for customers' Gusto companies
scenarios.when_this_applies: Your agent connects to Gusto companies outside your own organization, directly or via an approved Unified API partner.

hands_on.basis: estimate from step count, not measured; includes preparing security documents

prerequisites.title: Gusto Developer Account
prerequisites.detail: Sign up before filing the Production Pre-Approval application.

prerequisites.title: Security documentation ready
prerequisites.detail: Prepare audits such as SOC 2 Type 2, ISO 27001 or PCI DSS, pen test reports, and policies. Without a formal audit, you describe controls instead.

prerequisites.title: Security and incident response contacts
prerequisites.detail: You need a name, title and email for both contacts.

steps.title: Sign up for Gusto Developer Account
steps.detail: Create the account in the Developer Portal.
steps.done_when: You can log into the Developer Portal.

steps.title: Draft security documentation package
steps.detail: Collect and organize audits, pen tests, policies and contact details to match the questionnaire.
steps.done_when: Package is complete for the questionnaire.

steps.title: Submit Production Pre-Approval
steps.detail: File the application with business and legal details.

steps.title: Wait for Partnerships and Security Review
steps.detail: Partnerships reviews first; if approved, the GRC team starts the Security Review. Reply quickly to extra requests, since the review pauses.
steps.done_when: You receive approval email with next steps.

steps.title: Build and test against demo environment
steps.detail: Use api.gusto-demo.com, handle 2-hour token expiry and per-company OAuth.

steps.title: Create Composio auth config
steps.detail: Create a custom auth config with your own client ID and secret. Copy the redirect URI from the Composio dashboard into the Gusto portal.
steps.done_when: Auth config exists and a demo connection works.

steps.title: Pass QA and get production credentials
steps.detail: Gusto issues production credentials via the Developer Portal after QA.
steps.done_when: Production credentials appear in the portal.

traps.title: Production redirect changes need Gusto support
traps.detail: Demo redirect URIs are editable in the portal, but changing the production one requires emailing Gusto. Wildcards and fragments are not allowed.

traps.title: No production test accounts
traps.detail: All testing, before and after launch, must happen in the demo environment.

traps.title: Each company needs its own OAuth flow
traps.detail: Since v2023-05-01, tokens are restricted to one company, so multi-company admins repeat OAuth per company. Your app must handle this.

traps.title: Review pauses on unanswered requests
traps.detail: If Gusto asks for more information, the Security Review is on hold until you respond.

blockers.what_it_means: Production access is only available after approval and QA.
blockers.what_to_do: Complete pre-approval, Security Review and QA, then use the issued production credentials.
blockers.agent_can_help: Prepare the security documentation and a QA checklist.

blockers.what_it_means: Only primary admins or full access admins can enable a new application's access.
blockers.what_to_do: Ask the customer's primary or full access admin to complete the OAuth flow.

open_questions: How long do Pre-Approval and Security Review take? Ask Gusto's Partnerships team when applying.
Are there minimum customer or user counts to apply? Not found; confirm with the Partnerships team.
Is there a re-review after changes? Not found; ask Gusto.
Does Gusto verify redirect domains or require a specific consent screen setup? Not found; check in the Developer Portal.

evidence.question: C1

evidence.question: C1
evidence.quote: Managed auth enforces a 15-minute minimum polling interval; your own app can use shorter polling intervals where supported.
evidence.answer: Limit of the managed app: managed auth enforces a 15-minute minimum polling interval for polling triggers, while a developer's own app can use shorter intervals where supported (general, not Gusto-specific).

evidence.question: G9

evidence.question: G9

evidence.answer: The example redirect URI on your own domain is https://yourdomain.com/api/composio-redirect.

evidence.question: G9
evidence.quote: Your endpoint must return a **302 redirect**.
evidence.answer: Your proxy endpoint must return a 302 redirect to Composio, not follow the redirect server-side or make a fetch call to Composio.

evidence.question: G9
evidence.quote: The user's browser needs to be redirected so the OAuth flow completes correctly.
evidence.answer: The browser must be redirected, not the server, so the OAuth flow completes correctly.

evidence.question: G9
evidence.quote: During OAuth, the browser briefly redirects through `backend.composio.dev` so Composio can capture the auth token.
evidence.answer: Without a proxy, the browser briefly redirects through backend.composio.dev during OAuth so Composio can capture the auth token.

evidence.question: G9

evidence.answer: Some toolkits also display the Composio callback URL on the consent screen.

evidence.question: G9

evidence.answer: To hide Composio's domain, you can proxy the redirect through your own domain instead.

evidence.quote: This endpoint receives the OAuth callback and immediately 302-redirects it to Composio:

evidence.answer: By default, the provider consent screen (e.g., Google, GitHub) shows 'Composio wants to access your account'; the page's fix is to use your own OAuth app.

evidence.quote: Add your own OAuth app only for toolkits where the provider consent screen must show your brand.

evidence.answer: The callback URL to register with your own OAuth app, when proxying, is your own domain endpoint (example: https://yourdomain.com/api/composio-redirect).
